root_cause.text: The uacce driver's vm_operations_struct lacks an .mremap callback, so the kernel's default mremap behavior copies vm_private_data (pointing to the queue structure) to the new VMA, leading to duplicate uacce_vma_close calls on munmap and a double-free of q->qfr.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds uacce_vma_mremap that returns -EPERM to explicitly disable mremap, and the commit description explains that "the default mremap copies the original vma's vm_private_data (i.e., q) to the new vma, both munmap operations would trigger vma_close, causing q->qfr to be freed twice".

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent userspace from remapping UACCE virtual memory areas by implementing the mremap VMA operation to return -EPERM, thus protecting the device memory from unauthorized relocation.
intent_record.what: Added a new static function uacce_vma_mremap that returns -EPERM, and registered it as the .mremap handler in uacce_vm_ops.
intent_record.how: The mremap handler now explicitly denies any attempt to remap the VMA, preventing userspace from relocating the memory region associated with the UACCE device.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent userspace from remapping UACCE virtual memory areas by implementing the mremap VMA operation to return -EPERM, thus protecting the device memory from unauthorized relocation.

relevance_review.reason: The group implements the missing .mremap callback by returning -EPERM, directly preventing the default mremap behavior that causes the double-free vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This statement defines the vm_operations_struct without an .mremap callback, causing the kernel to use default mremap behavior that copies vm_private_data, leading to double-free.

This statement assigns the .close callback but does not provide an .mremap callback, so when userspace performs mremap, the default behavior duplicates the vm_private_data, resulting in multiple vma_close calls and potential double-free.
